External email-domain intelligence classifies 'yahoo.com' as a free webmail address, which is what most real cardholders and most fraudsters both use. Measured across the bank's closed cases this is the baseline -- it appears on 3,667 confirmed frauds and 573 cleared alarms -- so it is named as context and carries no weight.

Connected components over the device-sharing graph place this card in a bounded component of 2 cards (C00266-K1), linked transitively through device profiles each used by no more than 8 cards. A component this small is a genuine shared origin rather than a common configuration.

Known fraud pattern 5: Account takeover: Account takeover. Mixed-channel activity inconsistent with the cardholder, often with device and match-flag anomalies, pointing to stolen credentials rather than a stolen number.

case.summary: Monitoring sweep on card C09623-K2 identified a $549.96 in person transaction on 2016-11-06, against which 3 of the card-detail match flags M1-M9 came back F and step-up authentication was not completed. The $549.96 is 8.0x this card's median and above its 95th percentile, and the connected component of 2 cards (C00266-K1) indicates a genuine shared origin. The transaction was assessed as account takeover at probability 0.76 with $570.05 of exposure under case ID 5. Policy rule R6 named the shared element and recommended `CREATE_CASE`, `FILE_REPORT`, and `MONITOR_CONNECTED_CARDS` for the other card, while policy rule R8 recommended escalation because the exposure exceeded $500.

sar.narrative: On 2016-11-06, customer C09623 used card C09623-K2 to conduct 2 transaction(s) totaling $570.05, of which the triggering transaction was $549.96 on 2016-11-06 in person under product code W and billed in region 204.0. Three of the card-detail match flags M1-M9 came back F on this transaction, and step-up authentication was not completed. The activity was conducted in the same region as card C00266-K1, and connected components over the device-sharing graph placed C09623-K2 in a bounded component of 2 cards linked transitively through device profiles each used by no more than 8 cards, indicating a shared origin. On contact, no reply within 24 hours, which is an assumption recorded in the case file, as no cardholder replies were available to this investigation. The activity is suspicious because it is consistent with known fraud pattern 5, specifically account takeover involving mixed-channel activity inconsistent with the cardholder and pointing to stolen credentials rather than a stolen number, and the $549.96 amount is 8.0x this card's median and above its 95th percentile. The probability of fraud was assessed at 0.76, and the activity connects to a device profile shared with other compromised cards, which requires a report regardless of amount. The filing is supported by memory from 5 closed cases whose transaction most resembles this one—CC-1342, CC-4201, CC-5496, CC-4781, and CC-1596—which all closed as confirmed fraud (account takeover, out of region use), as well as by the baseline finding that the 'yahoo.com' email domain is a free webmail address carrying no weight. Because the evidence conflicts and the exposure of $570.05 exceeds $500, policy rule R8 mandates escalation to a fraud analyst, while policy rule R6 requires naming the shared element, creating a case, filing a report, and monitoring connected cards, and policy rule R4 requires declining the pending authorization and monitoring the card.

stop_reason: Policy 6: probability 0.76 on 3 independent pieces of evidence sits between the stopping thresholds, and the evidence-request budget is spent. The remaining uncertainty is the cardholder's own intent, which only the cardholder or an analyst can resolve; the recommended actions route it to them rather than resolving it in the graph.
